delivered: Mitigation proposal: Establish a closed-loop “screw-recovery/weight drift” control using only existing sensors (barrel thermocouples, cycle-time logger, and check-weigher). Mechanism: Treat the increasing screw recovery time and part weight drift as an indicator of degraded melt density/consistency and inconsistent back-off behavior; use the check-weigher output at the quality gate and the cycle-time logger’s recovery-time trend to detect drift, and automatically adjust the injection hold time/pressure setpoint and/or back-off speed to bring part weight back to target within the same barrel setpoints. Direction-of-effect: Increasing screw recovery time drives an increase in part weight; therefore, reducing back-off speed drives a decrease in screw recovery time, which in turn drives a decrease in part weight toward target. Implementation: 1) From the check-weigher, compute rolling average part weight and deviation from target; 2) From the cycle-time logger, compute rolling average screw recovery time and detect increases beyond a threshold; 3) When both conditions persist for a defined window, trigger a corrective action: reduce the back-off speed (to ensure more complete metering) and/or increase injection hold pressure slightly to stabilize density, while keeping barrel temperature setpoints unchanged; 4) Log the adjustments and verify with subsequent check-weigher readings that weight returns to target and recovery time stabilizes. Measures relied on: Existing sensors only—barrel thermocouples (to confirm no temperature drift is causing the issue), cycle-time logger (for recovery time monitoring), and check-weigher (for part weight feedback). No new instrumentation is added; the mitigation uses data fusion from these existing measurements to implement a simple feedback correction to process parameters (back-off speed/hold pressure) that affects part weight and screw recovery consistency. IMPLEMENTATION BILL: 1) Signal Source: Check-weigher output (part weight); 2) Signal Source: Cycle-time logger (screw recovery time); 3) Signal Source: Barrel zone thermocouples (barrel temperature); 4) Derived Input: Rolling average part weight deviation, derived from check-weigher output; 5) Derived Input: Rolling average screw recovery time, derived from cycle-time logger; 6) Action: Adjust back-off speed; 7) Action: Adjust injection hold pressure; 8) Verification: Subsequent check-weigher readings and cycle-time logger recovery time trends.
